summary: Revenue up 25% to $127.6B on a doubling of Google Cloud, but GAAP EPS of $2.12 missed ~$3.01 consensus, mainly because of an $8.7B loss on equity securities. Capex of $51.4B pushed free cash flow to -$9.1B and the stock fell about 12% the next day.

results.source: Alphabet 8-K Ex. 99.1 (prior year derived as OCF minus capex)

guidance: FY2026 capex guidance kept at $195-205B; through September Alphabet had spent $132.0B.
Capex expected to 'increase significantly' in 2027; details promised on the Q4 call.
Q4 revenue faces a larger FX headwind than Q3 (mainly Search and YouTube ads), and Search laps a late-2025 acceleration.
TPU system sales expected to scale in Q4, with the significant majority of that revenue landing in 2027.
highlights: Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7B and segment operating income tripled to $11.1B (about 36% margin).
Management said year-over-year Search query growth is the highest in five years.
Operating income grew 30% and operating margin reached 31.8% despite heavy depreciation and Alphabet-level costs.
External TPU systems sales contributed meaningfully to growth, with named customers including Apple for model pretraining.
lowlights: GAAP EPS fell to $2.12 from $2.87: an $8.7B loss on equity securities cut EPS by $0.55, and interest expense rose to $0.97B from $0.14B.
Search & other grew 12%, slower than 15% a year earlier, and was roughly flat quarter over quarter.
Free cash flow was negative for a second straight quarter (-$9.1B) as capex reached $51.4B.
No buybacks in the first nine months of 2026; Alphabet instead issued $12.4B of stock through its ATM program and $28.7B of notes in Q3.
Other Bets operating loss widened to $2.0B from $1.4B.
thesis_impact: Supports the Cloud pillar (ahead of plan) and the full-stack AI pillar; weakens the capex-return/FCF pillar, which is now at risk. Search is holding up but slowing. Net: thesis intact at medium conviction, with FCF recovery the key thing to watch on the Q4 call.
